title: Beyond the agreement paradigm: Regulating algorithmic collusion under the Competition Act, 2002
description: Antitrust laws presume a meeting of minds. Section 3(1) of the Competition Act, 2002 prohibits any agreement causing an appreciable adverse effect on competition, and Section 2(b) extends this to any “arrangement, understanding or action in concert.” Capacious as it is, that formulation did not anticipate pricing algorithms that, through reinforcement learning, collude autonomously without any human communication.The concern is empirically grounded.
